subjective: Clinical context for patient PAT_001: Subacute post-stroke rehabilitation assessment during standardized isometric knee extension evaluating persistent right-sided lower-limb weakness and progressive myoelectric fatigue. No additional patient-reported symptoms were documented.
objective: Muscle group evaluated: Quadriceps femoris (vastus lateralis). Dominant side: right. Left channel sEMG: RMS 123.6 uV, MDF 78.4 Hz, MNF 91.2 Hz, Fatigue Slope -0.32 Hz/s. Right channel sEMG: RMS 86.4 uV, MDF 61.8 Hz, MNF 73.5 Hz, Fatigue Slope -0.74 Hz/s. Bilateral Symmetry Index: 35.4%.
assessment: Bilateral sEMG amplitude analysis demonstrates pronounced bilateral amplitude asymmetry (Bilateral Symmetry Index 35.4%), with reduced recruitment amplitude on the right side (86.4 uV) relative to the left side (123.6 uV). Frequency-domain analysis reveals pronounced spectral compression consistent with progressive myoelectric fatigue, with median frequency values of 78.4 Hz (left) and 61.8 Hz (right) and fatigue slopes of -0.32 Hz/s (left) and -0.74 Hz/s (right). Interpretation is strictly limited to the recorded sEMG biomarkers and documented clinical context.
plan: Correlate objective sEMG findings for the Quadriceps femoris (vastus lateralis) with clinical physical examination by the supervising clinician. Perform serial follow-up sEMG reassessment under an identical testing protocol to monitor bilateral activation symmetry and myoelectric fatigue progression. Guide non-pharmacological rehabilitation or ergonomic load adjustments based on longitudinal neuromuscular response.
